mission.title: n8n: Bearer Authentication Not Working with HTTP Request Node Pagination
mission.description: When the HTTP Request node uses a predefined credential with Bearer Auth and pagination is enabled, the Authorization header is only sent on the first request. Subsequent paginated requests are missing the Bearer token, so the API responds with 401 "Unauthorized" on page 2 and beyond.

steps.title: Reproduce the 401 on paginated requests
steps.description:
In the n8n editor, open the failing workflow's HTTP Request node. It is configured with Authentication: "Predefined Credential Type" (e.g. Bearer Auth) and Options > Pagination enabled. Execute the node: the first request succeeds, but the second page fails with `401 - "Unauthorized"`. If n8n runs in Kubernetes, confirm the error in the logs:
```bash
kubectl logs -l app.kubernetes.io/name=n8n -n n8n --tail=100 | grep -i "unauthorized\|401"
```

steps.title: Confirm the Authorization header is dropped on page 2+
steps.description:
Point the node at a request inspector (e.g. a local echo server) or enable debug logging to compare requests:
```bash
kubectl set env deployment/n8n -n n8n N8N_LOG_LEVEL=debug
kubectl logs -l app.kubernetes.io/name=n8n -n n8n -f | grep -i "authorization\|pagination"
```
The first request includes `Authorization: Bearer <token>`; the follow-up requests built from the pagination options do not. This confirms the pagination mechanism is not re-applying the predefined credential's auth header.

steps.title: Add the Authorization header explicitly to the node's header parameters
Alternatively, set the Authorization header in the pagination request options
Verify all pages return 200
steps.description:
Re-execute the node and confirm every paginated request now succeeds and returns the full result set instead of failing after page 1:
```bash
kubectl logs -l app.kubernetes.io/name=n8n -n n8n --tail=50 --since=5m | grep -i "401\|unauthorized"
```
No further 401 errors should appear, and the node output should contain items from all pages.

resolution.summary: The fix works because the paginated follow-up requests are built from the node's pagination options, and the root cause is that this request-building path does not re-apply the predefined credential's authentication — the Bearer token is attached only to the initial request and is dropped from every subsequent page request, producing 401 errors. Setting the Authorization header explicitly — as a node header parameter, via a Generic "Header Auth" credential, or as a header-type parameter inside the pagination options — puts the token into the request definition itself, so it is sent on every page request. Because {{ $credentials }} expressions are not available in node parameters, the token must be provided directly in the header value. Source: https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/issues/16005

prerequisites.description: A running Kubernetes cluster with n8n installed or the issue environment reproducible.
